funder.quote: Alle norske bedrifter må ha minst 500 000 kroner i total egenkapital ved søketidspunktet.
funder.says: the amount is in KRONER, and the quantity it bounds is equity, not the balance-sheet total.

fx.rate_source: European Central Bank euro foreign exchange reference rates

why: three faults on one row and the currency is only the third. (1) comparator.ts's `numeric_gte` opens with `typeof answer === "number"` and balanceBand is answered with one of "<2M" | "2-43M" | ">43M", so this spec has never evaluated for any founder and never could. (2) the rule bounds TOTAL EQUITY CAPITAL -- what the owners have put in -- and balanceBand is the balance-sheet TOTAL; the two differ by every liability the company carries, and we do not ask for equity. (3) the threshold 500000 is the funder's kroner numeral stored as if it were euro: NOK 500,000 is about EUR 46,000, an eleven-fold overstatement. No conversion repairs (1) or (2), so there is no band to write.

funder.quote: Forskningsorganisasjoner uten rammebevilgning kan få utbetalt maksimalt 500 000 kroner i støtte fra ordningen per år.
funder.says: the cap is NOK 500,000 -- about EUR 46,000 -- and it binds only RESEARCH ORGANISATIONS WITHOUT A FRAMEWORK GRANT.

fx.rate_source: European Central Bank euro foreign exchange reference rates

why: the conversion is stable and would give band_max b25k_100k, three bands below the stored b100k_500k. IT IS STILL NOT WRITTEN, because the sentence's own first five words scope it: 'Forskningsorganisasjoner UTEN RAMMEBEVILGNING'. The same page says organisations WITH a framework grant apply through a different call entirely. assessInstrument conjoins every filter, so encoding the subset's cap tests it against every Norwegian founder, and a EUR 100k ceiling applied to a population it does not bind is a worse product than no ceiling. wsIC's test decides it: name the intake field that says which branch a founder is in. Holding a framework grant from the Research Council is not one, and cannot be asked.

funder.says: the floor is NOK 1,000,000, not EUR 1,000,000, and not EUR 500,000 either.

fx.rate_source: European Central Bank euro foreign exchange reference rates

why: THE ONLY GATE THE PROPERTY ITSELF REFUSES, and no judgement of mine is involved. NOK 1,000,000 is EUR 81,193 at the decade's weakest krone and EUR 113,546 at its strongest, and the intake's band edge sits at EUR 100,000 between them. A band chosen today would be a different verdict next year with no record of why, so there is no band to choose. Separately: the stored floor b500k_2m5 is two bands above even the spot conversion, and a band_min EXCLUDES everyone below it -- so this gate has been shutting out founders asking EUR 100k-EUR 500k from a scheme whose own floor is about EUR 92k.

IT IS STILL NOT WRITTEN. `satr_hu_rnd` is a FAMILY-tier record aggregating EUR 732M over 3,821 awards, and the quote comes off page 1 of a single GINOP Plusz call PDF whose name does not even match the gate's own `source_file` (hu_nkfi_alap_380_2014_korm_rendelet.html). Writing the true ceiling of one call onto a whole national R&D family would newly obstruct 819 of the 897 held-out founders -- everyone who answered b500k_2m5 -- on the strength of one page. why: the conversion is stable and would move this ceiling to '<2M'. IT IS NOT WRITTEN, because the funder's sentence is a DISJUNCTION and the corpus holds it as two gates -- turnover here, balance sheet on the sibling -- which assessInstrument conjoins. Tightening both legs of an OR that is evaluated as an AND turns a company that satisfies Vinnova on one leg into a company we obstruct on the other, and the true SEK bound is tighter than the stored euro one, so the correction would widen exactly that false exclusion. funder.says: the minimum grant is PLN 150,000 -- about EUR 34,700 -- unconditionally, with no branch and no subset.

fx.rate_source: European Central Bank euro foreign exchange reference rates

why: THE ONE GATE WHERE THE CURRENCY IS THE ONLY THING WRONG. The sentence is unconditional, the instrument is a leaf programme with its own source URL, the conversion is stable across the decade (EUR 30,288 to EUR 36,314, all inside b25k_100k), and the operator and the field are both right. Moving the floor from b100k_500k to b25k_100k REMOVES a false exclusion and adds none: every founder who passes today still passes, and founders asking EUR 25k-EUR 100k stop being shut out of a scheme whose own floor is EUR 35k. Nothing is widened to make a conversion fit -- b25k_100k is the band the funder's own number lands in.

funder.quote: not have gross assets worth more than £30 million before any shares are issued, and not more than £35 million immediately afterwards
funder.says: the ceiling is GBP 30 million of gross assets.

fx.rate_source: European Central Bank euro foreign exchange reference rates

why: THE BAND DOES NOT MOVE, AND RECORDING THAT IS THE POINT. GBP 30 million is about EUR 35.1 million and lands in '2-43M', the band already stored -- and it lands there at every rate sterling has held in ten years, from EUR 32.3M to EUR 36.4M. This is the whole reason the class went unseen: sterling at 1.17 is absorbed by bands four and five times wider than the error, so the only currency anybody was likely to notice is the only one that mostly comes out right. The write changes value_spec by nothing and encoding_method to `fx_converted`, so the row states that its band was checked against the funder's currency rather than being right by luck.
